## Desired behavior

Gazebo's `Mesh` data structure is currently defined in [gz-common's graphics/include/gz/common/Mesh.hh](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-common/blob/main/graphics/include/gz/common/Mesh.hh). This data structure is simple enough that it could be hosted in `gz-math`, which would make the `Mesh` representation available to `sdformat`, though loading and other mesh operations that require other dependencies would likely remain in gz-common.

I've opened this feature request to discuss whether a Mesh representation in gz-math would be useful and how much effort the migration would require in order to make a cost-benefit analysis.

## Alternatives considered

Keep the Mesh definition in `gz-common`.

new_candidates.body:
### Description

### What happens

A single `rep.orchestrator.step()` takes four application updates. With sensors on
autotrigger (`omni:sensor:tickRate = 0`, the default) every application update renders
every render product, so a capture that keeps one image per camera pays for four.

Three of the four are not wanted as images:

| Update | Purpose | Image used? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | publish the scheduled capture time | no |
| 2 | produce the frame | **yes** |
| 3, 4 | let the host-side writer queue drain | no |

In a path-traced configuration with `spp == totalSpp` each update is a complete,
converged render, so **75% of the cost of a capture is discarded pixels**.

### Where it comes from

`omni/replicator/core/scripts/orchestrator.py`, extension `omni.replicator.core-1.13.36+110.3.0`.

**The two flush updates**, line 1991:

```python
elif dispatcher and _needs_multitick_post_render_flush:
    for _ in range(2):
        await omni.kit.app.get_app().next_update_async()
```

Taken whenever multi-tick rendering is enabled and the timeline is playing:

```python
_needs_multitick_post_render_flush = _multitick_rate_enabled and _orchestrator._timeline.is_playing()
```

The sibling flush a few lines above explains the intent: *"host-side render vars and
writer schedule events are only observable on later rendered updates"*. The requirement
is elapsed updates, not pixels, but on autotrigger sensors each one renders.

**The scheduling update**, line 1910:

```python
while attempts < MAX_STEP_ATTEMPTS and (
    not _orchestrator._sim_times_to_write
    or (_orchestrator.status == Status.STEPPING
        and cur_sim_time == _get_time(*_orchestrator._sim_times_to_write[-1]))
):
    attempts += 1
    await omni.kit.app.get_app().next_update_async()
```

This needs at least one update by construction. With two GPUs it needs two, because the
orchestrator observes the new capture time one update later.

### Measured

Ten cameras, 1944x1204, path tracing at 32 spp, `spp == totalSpp`, one RTX 6000 Ada,
Isaac Sim 6.1.0-rc.26. Timeline playing, which is required by our character animation.

| Configuration | Updates per capture | s per captured frame |
|---|---|---|
| default | 4 | 60.3 |
| `--/rtx/hydra/supportMultiTickRate=false` | 2 | 29.6 |

Removing the two flush updates halves the frame. Outputs were compared file by file
across ten frames and ten cameras: rgb, depth and semantic segmentation byte-identical.

### What we expected

That the number of full renders per capture matches the number of captures requested.

Two things would fix it, both inside Replicator:

1. **The flush should not render.** It needs updates to elapse so writer schedule events
   become observable; it does not need images. Either skip it when nothing is waiting on
   it, or advance the application without driving the render graph.
2. **Publishing the scheduled capture time should not cost a render**, and should not
   cost two of them when more than one GPU is present.

### Workaround and its cost

Launching with `--/rtx/hydra/supportMultiTickRate=false` removes the flush, which is the
50% above. It is not free: the documentation states that most code paths in 6.0 assume
the global default, and the same setting also relaxes the render-wait loop, which
otherwise requires the SDG dispatcher's compute count to have advanced.

Per-sensor tick rates are the other obvious route and do not work here: a camera with a
rate may skip the very update the capture is waiting for, so one image is silently lost
and the writers renumber rather than leave a gap. That matches the answer in
https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/different-sensors-with-different-frequencies/312398
("this is currently not a supported feature").

### Isaac Sim version

6.1.0-rc.26+release.49347.2d230af4.gl

### Operating System (OS)

Ubuntu 24.04, CUDA 13.0

### GPU Name

RTX 6000 Ada

### GPU Driver and CUDA versions

Driver 580.95.05, Cuda 12.4

### Logs

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce issue

This is an flaky test regression observed on the buildfarm job `nightly_win_rep`. It has not been reproduced locally:
1. On Windows, build ROS 2 Rolling from source (rcl at `rolling`) with RTI Connext DDS 7.7.0 and `rmw_connextdds`.
2. Run the test repeatedly until it fails:
   ```
   set RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_connextdds
   colcon test --packages-select rcl --ctest-args -R test_events__rmw_connextdds --retest-until-fail 30
   ```
   or run `test_events` with `--gtest_filter=TestEventFixture.test_pubsub_liveliness_kill_pub --gtest_repeat=50`.
3. Check for the failed liveliness assertions at `test_events.cpp` lines 630 to 633.


### Expected behavior

The subscription liveliness event reports the lease expiry (`not_alive_count == 1`) in every run.

### Actual behavior

`TestEventFixture.test_pubsub_liveliness_kill_pub` (`rcl/test/rcl/test_events.cpp`, ctest target `test_events__rmw_connextdds`) intermittently fails on Windows. After the publisher's liveliness lease should have expired, the subscription liveliness event still reports the publisher as alive:

- `alive_count` is 1 (expected 0)
- `alive_count_change` is 1 (expected 0)
- `not_alive_count` is 0 (expected 1)
- `not_alive_count_change` is 0 (expected 1)

(assertions at `test_events.cpp` lines 630 to 633). It failed in 12 of the last 30 `nightly_win_rep` builds, including a streak of `#4284` to `#4286`.


### Additional information


#### Reference builds
- https://ci.ros2.org/job/nightly_win_rep/4286/ (`Test #24: test_events__rmw_connextdds ...***Failed 8.08 sec`)
- https://ci.ros2.org/job/nightly_win_rep/4285/
- https://ci.ros2.org/job/nightly_win_rep/4284/

#### Failing tests
<details><summary>Failing tests</summary>

- `rcl.TestEventFixture.test_pubsub_liveliness_kill_pub`
- `projectroot.test.test_events__rmw_connextdds` (ctest target, same failure at ctest level)

</details>

#### Flakiness (30 days)

| Job Name | Last Fail | First Fail | Build Count | Failure Count | Failure Percentage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| nightly_win_rep | 2026-11-09 | 2026-10-10 | 24 | 13 | 54.17 |

#### Log output
<details><summary>Build#4286 gtest output</summary>

```
[ RUN      ] TestEventFixture.test_pubsub_liveliness_kill_pub
W:\src\ros2\rcl\rcl\test\rcl\test_events.cpp(630): error: Expected equality of these values:
  liveliness_status.alive_count
    Which is: 1
  0
test_events.cpp(631): error: ... liveliness_status.alive_count_change Which is: 1 (expected 0)
test_events.cpp(632): error: ... liveliness_status.not_alive_count Which is: 0 (expected 1)
test_events.cpp(633): error: ... liveliness_status.not_alive_count_change Which is: 0 (expected 1)
[  FAILED  ] TestEventFixture.test_pubsub_liveliness_kill_pub (2211 ms)
```

</details>

<details><summary>Test source (rolling), relevant lines</summary>

```
constexpr seconds LIVELINESS_LEASE_DURATION_IN_S = 1s;
constexpr seconds MAX_WAIT_PER_TESTCASE = 10s;
...
ret = rcl_publish(&publisher, &msg, nullptr);       // one message, publisher is not destroyed
std::this_thread::sleep_for(2 * LIVELINESS_LEASE_DURATION_IN_S);
... conditional_wait_for_msgs_and_events(context_ptr, MAX_WAIT_PER_TESTCASE, all_ready, ...)
ret = rcl_take_event(&subscription_event, &liveliness_status);
EXPECT_EQ(liveliness_status.alive_count, 0);
EXPECT_EQ(liveliness_status.alive_count_change, 0);
EXPECT_EQ(liveliness_status.not_alive_count, 1);
EXPECT_EQ(liveliness_status.not_alive_count_change, 1);
```

</details>

#### Analysis notes
- The 2211 ms test duration is almost exactly the fixed `2 * lease` sleep (2 s), so the lease expiry was not reflected in the event by the time it was taken.
- The failure is specific to `rmw_connextdds` in these builds; cyclonedds (Passed 5.52 s) and fastrtps (Passed 4.95 s) passed in `#4286`.
- Claude's Hypothesis (not verified): on a loaded Windows container, Connext has not processed the lease expiry within the fixed 2 s sleep, so the event still carries the earlier "alive" state. The wait returns as soon as the event is ready, so it can succeed before the expiry is delivered. No Connext-side timestamps are available to confirm this.
